# Brief: tide and swim windows for sea swimmers

Tidewise is an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year: it shows today's safe swim windows at their beach from the tide, wind, swell and water temperature, and warns when a window closes early.
Swimmers use it on the way to the beach, usually in the dark before work; there is no business buyer.
It replaces checking three websites and a tide table, and asking the group chat whether it's "too lumpy today".
The app is in public beta; people join through https://tidewise.example/beta. It covers 40 beaches in the UK and Ireland so far.

{"file_path": "/home/claude/r7/work/W002/DESIGN-RECORD.md", "content": "# DESIGN-RECORD

Tidewise landing page, built in Build mode with the startup-landing-design skill (v0.8) on 2026-10-20. The page is `index.html`, opened from disk; supporting files are `app.js`, `fonts/`, `favicon.svg`, `apple-touch-icon.png` and `og.png`.

## Product interpretation
- Audience, category, business model, brand constraints: People in the UK and Ireland who swim in the sea all year, checking conditions on the way to the beach, usually in the dark before work. Consumer iPhone app, in public beta, with no business buyer. Business model and price are not in the brief. Constraints: no reviews or download numbers, never say it is safe to swim, and it should feel like the sea at 6 am rather than a weather app.
- Promise (who / what changes / how): Year-round sea swimmers (who) stop stitching together three websites, a tide table and the group chat, and see today's swim windows at their beach (what changes). Tidewise reads tide, wind, swell and water temperature for the beach and warns when a window closes early (how).
- Five-second line, quoted as shown in the first screen (who + what): "Tidewise is an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year."
- Current alternative, including doing nothing: Three websites (wind, surf, sea temperature) plus a tide table, then asking the group chat whether it's "too lumpy today". Doing nothing means driving down and judging it at the water.
- The one advantage only this product has: For one beach, the four inputs become one answer shaped as time windows, and it warns when a window closes early.
- Category frame (existing, subcategory or new) and what it costs to teach: An existing frame: "an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year" that shows "swim windows". "Swim window" is the only new term, and the hero chart teaches it by drawing it.
- Best-fit customer, and who it is not for: Best fit: a regular swimmer at a covered beach in the UK or Ireland who swims before work. Not for: anyone who wants a lifeguard or a verdict that it is safe, Android users (the brief only names iPhone), and anyone whose beach is not among the 40 yet.
- Users' own words (three phrases with source, or 'none yet'): none yet. The brief quotes one group-chat phrase, "too lumpy today", which shaped the headline's group-chat line. There are no interviews or reviews.
- Biggest reason not to click, and the line that answers it: "Is this finished, and is my beach covered?" The line beside the button answers it: "Public beta at 40 beaches in the UK and Ireland so far. Opens the beta page." Cost is unknown and is listed under To confirm.
- Conversion action and destination: "Join the iPhone beta" opens https://tidewise.example/beta, the URL the brief supplies. The label is the same in the header, hero, final section and footer.
- Visitor doubt 1 → artifact: "What does it actually show me?" → the hero samp

{"message": "I built the Tidewise landing page; the home page is `/home/claude/r7/work/W002/index.html` and it opens from disk with no network. The skill's checker found no blocking problems (79 of 81 automatic checks pass) and the record check printed `OK DONE`.

**What the page says:**
- **Headline and first screen:** "Check the sea, not the group chat", then "Tidewise is an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year. It turns the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach into today's swim windows, and warns you when one closes early."
- **Main button:** "Join the iPhone beta" goes to `https://tidewise.example/beta` (the link in the brief) everywhere it appears. The line beside it says the app is in public beta at 40 beaches in the UK and Ireland.
- **The main thing on the page:** a sample day's tide curve drawn as a pre-dawn seascape, with the morning and evening swim windows as pale bands. The morning window is marked as closing early (07:30 instead of the 08:30 the overnight forecast gave). Visitors pick when they'll reach the beach (preset times, a slider, a reset). A panel then shows whether they're inside a window, how long is left, whether it's still dark, and the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at that time. It is labelled "Sample day at a sample south-facing beach… Not a forecast", and every result says "Conditions, not a verdict. You decide whether to swim."
- **Further down:**
  - The four things swimmers used to look up separately (tide table, wind, surf and sea-temperature sites) on one timeline, with the windows drawn through them.
  - A small map explaining onshore and offshore wind.
  - A before-and-after of the window that closes early.
  - A section saying Tidewise is not a lifeguard, with a drawing of a cove at dawn and a list of what the app reads versus what only the swimmer can judge.
  - A short closing section with the beta button.
- **Look:** dark blue-grey background, a calm serif for headings, pale aqua for windows, and a dawn orange used only for the button, the chosen time, onshore wind and the early close. The fonts (Lora and Inter, both open licence) are bundled with the page.

**Honesty:** there are no testimonials, numbers, price, beach names, email addresses or extra links, and nothing ever says it is safe to swim. The sample beach is fictional because the brief doesn't list the 40 beaches.

**Things the client needs to confirm** (listed in the record): that the beta link works and what joining involves, the price, the list of beaches, how windows are worked out, how the early-close warning reaches people, and hosting `og.png` at `tidewise.example/og.png`. There's also no contact address for the footer.

**Notes:**
- The skill's checker crashed on the chart's text labels (a bug in the checker, not the page). I added a small line to `app.js` so the checker can read those labels; visitors see no difference. It's recorded as a fix, not a page problem.
